name: Localbahnmuseum Innsbruck (Tiroler Museumsbahnen)
kurzbeschreibung: The Localbahnmuseum in the old Stubaitalbahnhof in Innsbruck: historic trams, locomotives, and Tyrolean railway heritage since 1891.
beschreibung:
Overview

The steeped-in-history Localbahnmuseum Innsbruck – operated by the association Tiroler Museumsbahnen (TMB) – is situated at the foot of the Bergisel in the Innsbruck district of Wilten at Pater-Reinisch-Weg 4, at an altitude of approximately 590 metres. Housed in the heritage-listed train sheds and workshop rooms of the former Stubaitalbahnhof from 1904, this specialized museum ranks among Central Europe's most significant railway history collections. It documents the pioneering development of Tyrolean alpine valleys through electric local railways, rack railways, and tramways from the late 19th century onwards.

Vehicle Collection & History of Technology

The origins of the collection date back to 1983, when railway enthusiasts founded the association dedicated to preserving historic Tyrolean rail vehicles. The exhibition hall houses more than 25 historic original rail vehicles, lovingly restored to working order by dedicated volunteers. Among the highlights are railcars of the legendary Stubaitalbahn – the world's first single-phase high-voltage alternating current railway line (opened in 1904) –, historic tramcars of the Innsbruck tram system, the Innsbrucker Mittelgebirgsbahn (Line 6), and rolling stock from the Rittner Bahn and Bozner Straßenbahn. Display panels, historic photographs, vintage ticket-printing machines, uniforms, railway signaling boards, and detailed model railway layouts illustrate the immense engineering achievements of alpine railway construction during the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy. On select summer weekends, the museum organizes nostalgia trips aboard vintage tram trains through the urban area of Innsbruck.

Visit & Getting There

The Localbahnmuseum Innsbruck is open to visitors during the summer months from early May to late October on Saturdays from 09:00 to 17:00 (guided tours for groups of 10 or more are available year-round on weekdays upon prior reservation). Admission prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €3.00, toddlers free; family ticket approx. €14.00. Admission is free with the Innsbruck Card. Getting there by public transport: from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof take tram line 1 to the Bergisel stop, or take the Stubaitalbahn (STB) directly to the Stubaitalbahnhof stop (only a one-minute walk to the museum). By car: via the Brennerautobahn A13 (exit Innsbruck Süd), with parking available at the Bergiselschanze ski jump or along Pater-Reinisch-Weg.

Tips

The historic vehicle hall and workshop rooms feature stepless access and are wheelchair accessible; narrow access steps lead into some of the historic carriages. For railway enthusiasts and children, climbing onto the wooden slatted benches of the vintage trams is an unforgettable experience. Pair your visit with a panoramic journey on the scenic Stubaitalbahn across the Telfer Wiesen meadows to Fulpmes.
preis: Erwachsene ca. 6,00 €, Kinder ca. 3,00 €; mit Innsbruck Card kostenlos
oeffnungszeiten: Mai bis Okt samstags 09:00–17:00 Uhr (Gruppen auf Anfrage ganzjährig)
